channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Ransomware Groups Multiply Despite Fewer Victim Payments
item.description: Check Point Research’s State of Ransomware Q3 2026 report lists 2,830 victims on data-leak sites, the highest quarterly total on record. July, August, and September accounted for 964, 1,042, and 824 victims respectively, indicating a sustained expansion of active ransomware groups. The report shows declining payments but continued brand proliferation, stressing the need for stronger defensive measures.

item.title: AWS European Sovereign Cloud: Architecture and Compliance Overview
item.description: AWS European Sovereign Cloud offers infrastructure designed to meet European data sovereignty requirements, providing isolated regions and compliance with local regulations. The architecture provides physical and logical separation, encryption controls, and audit capabilities, enabling organizations to retain full data control while leveraging AWS services. Customers can evaluate the platform against certifications and compliance frameworks to determine suitability for sensitive workloads.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Cockpit Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued an Important security update for the cockpit component on Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. The advisory cites several CVEs with CVSS scores, but no specific CVE ID is listed. Administrators should apply the cockpit update immediately to mitigate the identified vulnerabilities and consult the CVE links for detailed impact.

item.title: OpenAI, Cisco Launch AI-Assisted Linux Shield Tool
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco unveiled Shirudo, an AI-assisted Linux runtime that deploys temporary eBPF controls to block exploit behaviors before patches. The system generates programs that intercept vulnerable system calls, preventing exploitation without rebooting and narrowing the exposure window. Deploy Shirudo on exposed hosts, monitor logs, and apply vendor patches promptly to eliminate the root flaw.

item.title: CISA Adds N-able MailAssure SSRF to KEV Catalog
item.description: CISA added a server-side request forgery flaw in N-able MailAssure’s LDAP to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, noting active exploitation. CVE-2026-134624, scored 9.3, lets attackers force the server to request arbitrary internal resources, exposing data or enabling lateral movement. Administrators should apply the latest patch immediately and enforce LDAP restrictions to mitigate SSRF risk.

item.title: OpenAI, Cisco Release Shirudo to Shield Linux Until Patches
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, a Linux runtime that deploys temporary eBPF controls to block exploit behaviors while patches are pending. Shirudo generates small programs that intercept vulnerable system calls, preventing exploitation without rebooting and narrowing the exposure window. Deploy Shirudo on exposed hosts, monitor logs, and apply vendor patches promptly to eliminate the root flaw.

item.title: IT Delegates Password Management While Maintaining Control
item.description: IT departments often delegate password management to business units, creating accounts that may be unknown to central security teams. This practice can leave IT responsible for credentials it cannot monitor, increasing risk when personnel changes or external contractors access shared accounts. Implementing centralized identity governance, enforcing least-privilege access, and requiring IT involvement in account provisioning can mitigate these risks.

item.title: Stalwart 1.2.0 Adds Full Exchange Protocol Support
item.description: Stalwart 1.2.0 introduces full Exchange-compatible protocols, enabling MAPI over HTTP, EWS, ActiveSync, and Autodiscover for Outlook, Apple Mail, and mobile clients. The open-source mail server ships under the AGPL Community edition, offering mail, calendar, contacts, tasks, and notes. Administrators can deploy Stalwart as a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange, but should evaluate compatibility with existing client configurations before migration.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco Release Shirudo to Block Linux Exploits
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source AI-driven tool that blocks specific exploits on live Linux servers while teams test and deploy permanent patches. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield prevented a Java4Shell exploit against Elasticsearch without service interruption. Security teams should deploy Shirudo immediately to mitigate known exploits and reduce patch deployment windows.

item.title: Ongoing Scanning Detected on BANATSYNC Subnet
item.description: SANS Internet Storm Center reports continuous scanning from subnet 109.160.32.0/24, assigned to BANATSYNC SRL, a Romanian web hosting and VPS provider. DShield sensor data shows persistent probing over 90 days, suggesting ongoing reconnaissance or potential exploitation attempts against the subnet's hosts. Security teams should monitor for suspicious activity, enforce rate limiting, and harden hosts to mitigate potential threats.

item.title: Cybersecurity Jobs Open Now, November 24, 2026
item.description: A new Applied Cyber, Detections role is listed by Help Net Security, targeting remote positions in the United States. Candidates will support detection operations, develop and refine detection logic, and automate alert triage across web domains, social media, and other digital channels. The posting encourages collaboration with engineering and product teams to enhance detection capabilities and address evolving cyber threats.

item.title: USN-9189-1: Qt5Compat vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Qt5Compat did not correctly handle certain text codec names, which could lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service.

item.title: Chrome 158 Released for Android
item.description: Google has released Chrome 158 (158.0.8127.92) for Android, which will appear on Google Play within days. The update focuses on stability and performance enhancements, while incorporating the same security fixes present in the corresponding desktop releases for Windows, Mac, and Linux. Users should install the new package via Google Play; no additional work-around is required.

item.title: Red Hat issues python-oauthlib security update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python-oauthlib on RHEL 9, addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities. The update mitigates flaws that could enable remote code execution or privilege escalation, with CVSS scores linked via CVE references and rated Important by Product Security. Administrators should apply RHSA-2026:102668 immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: Aurora stops ClickFix attacks with intent detection
item.description: ClickFix attacks coerce users into executing malicious commands, creating a gray zone that evades traditional security tools. Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection employs intent-based detection to recognize execution patterns, stopping attacks at the moment they occur and mapping activity for visibility. Security teams can integrate Aurora to gain real-time protection against ClickFix and similar command-execution threats.

item.title: OT Gateways Reveal Authentication Status, Many Unprotected
item.description: Industrial serial gateways reveal whether they are authenticated, exposing a flaw in critical OT access devices. The default configuration broadcasts authentication status, allowing attackers to identify unprotected devices; no exploit is needed, but the disclosure raises credential theft risk. Disable status broadcasts, enforce authentication, and apply vendor firmware updates that conceal authentication state.

item.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Target .NET Developers
item.description: Socket researchers identified 13 malicious NuGet packages that lure .NET developers with fake job assessment prompts. The packages perform DLL side-loading, steal credentials, and embed GitHub-based malware, compromising developer environments. Security teams should audit package sources, enforce trusted feeds, and apply the latest .NET security updates to mitigate exposure and monitor for suspicious activity.

item.title: AWS SSM Agent default key flaw exposes role credentials
item.description: Amazon SSM Agent on AWS Windows Server AMIs contains a flaw where instances share a default cryptographic key during registration. CVE-2026-134069 allows a local non-admin user to retrieve the instance’s Default Host Management Configuration role credentials, enabling potential credential theft. AWS recommends updating to the latest SSM Agent version or applying the provided patch to eliminate the shared key vulnerability.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Golang Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a golang update for RHEL 10, fixing multiple security bugs in the Go compiler and runtime. The update addresses several CVE-linked issues, each with a CVSS base score indicating moderate impact; no active exploitation is known. Red Hat advises applying the update via the package manager; no workaround is needed.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Golang Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the golang runtime on RHEL 9, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates unspecified bugs that could allow local privilege escalation or code execution, with CVSS scores available via referenced CVE links. Administrators should apply the golang package update immediately to maintain system integrity.

item.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Zscaler for AI Security Integration
item.description: CrowdStrike announced a $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler, merging endpoint protection with zero-trust network security. The integration aims to centralize AI agent oversight, enabling unified threat detection across device and network layers. Customers will receive combined platform capabilities, but must plan for migration and potential licensing adjustments, ensuring seamless transition.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Python 3.6 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the python36:3.6 module on RHEL 8, addressing several vulnerabilities. The patch fixes bugs that could enable local privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution, with CVSS scores provided via CVE references. System administrators should install the updated python36 package promptly to secure their environments.

item.title: Aurora ADTP Blocks Modern Attacks by Continuous Behavior Tracking
item.description: Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection (ADTP) monitors endpoint activity to counter attacks that bypass conventional defenses. By linking related behaviors into a full attack narrative, ADTP identifies malicious intent before execution, enabling real-time disruption. Security teams should deploy ADTP alongside existing endpoint solutions and configure behavior thresholds for optimal coverage, reducing blind spots.

item.title: KEPCO Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Customer Records
item.description: A threat actor breached KEPCO’s internal network, accessing two systems that stored customer, employee, and contractor data. The intrusion leveraged an undisclosed vulnerability in the company’s network perimeter, enabling unauthorized data exfiltration and potential credential compromise. KEPCO has issued a security advisory and is conducting a forensic investigation, urging affected users to monitor accounts and change passwords.

item.title: Chrome Stable Channel Updated to 158.0.8127.88
item.description: Google Chrome released a stable channel update to version 158.0.8127.88 for Windows, Mac, and Linux, rolling out over the next weeks. The update includes security fixes, with a detailed change log available; users are encouraged to review the log before upgrading. Administrators should schedule the rollout, verify compatibility, and monitor for any post-upgrade issues via the community help forum.

item.title: Chrome Extended Stable Channel Updated to 156.0.8078.114
item.description: Google Chrome’s Extended Stable channel updated to 156.0.8078.114 for Windows and macOS, extending the stable release schedule. The update lists changes, with security fixes pending a later release, and will roll out over the next days or weeks. Users may review the change log, file bugs, or use the community forum while awaiting the security patch.

item.title: CVE-2026-134056 - Out-of-bounds write in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-196-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 12:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-134056, an out-of-bounds write issue in AWS-LC's padded block cipher decryption. If the output buffer is the minimum documented size, AWS-LC can write one byte past its end. The aws-lc-rs StreamingDecryptingKey API has a similar issue with cbc_pkcs7 and ecb_pkcs7.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important SQLite Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for SQLite on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores linked to each CVE in the advisory references. Administrators should apply the update immediately and verify that SQLite components are patched to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Cisco Products Affected by PHP Remote Code Vulnerability
item.description: Cisco products are vulnerable to a PHP flaw that permits remote code execution, as disclosed by the PHP Foundation on November 19, 2026. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-126714 and dubbed phpAfterShell, carries a Critical security impact rating and is referenced by GHSA-fm2m-fjf5-v3cp. Cisco recommends applying the available PHP security patches immediately to mitigate the RCE risk and ensure system integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Moderate Update for go-toolset:rhel8
item.description: Red Hat released a moderate security update for the go-toolset:rhel8 module on RHEL8, fixing multiple Go compiler bugs. The patch addresses local privilege escalation and denial-of-service flaws with CVSS scores up to 7.5, though no active exploitation is known. Red Hat advises applying the update via the standard RHEL8 update channel; no workarounds are required.

item.title: Trump Names Industry Veteran Davies as Acting Cyber Director
item.description: Trump appointed Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director, signaling a shift toward industry expertise amid outages and geopolitical tensions. The move follows criticism of cyber leadership and aims to leverage Davies' private sector experience to strengthen U.S. cyber defenses. The appointment is expected to influence policy direction and coordination with industry partners, though no immediate operational changes have been announced.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes AI Providers for Data Handling Violations
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI providers after discovering they violated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive user prompts and secrets. The policy breach leaked proprietary prompts, potentially compromising client confidentiality and violating OpenRouter's privacy commitments. OpenRouter suspended the providers, issued a public notice, and is reviewing vetting procedures to prevent future violations.
